Linus and Luke discuss Wikipedia’s decision to block Archive.today links, unpacking the security risks, alleged data tampering, and why trust is everything for archival services. They contrast Archive.today with the Internet Archive, debate the ethics of paywall circumvention, and reflect on how broken archives undermine journalism, accountability, and the historical record.

Linus and Luke discuss the disappearance of “third places,” why modern life pushes people into isolation, and how phones, cost of space, and social friction all play a role. They explore a hypothetical membership-based hangout designed to reduce decision paralysis, encourage parallel play, and bring people together while acknowledging the very real social and cultural challenges that might make it fail anyway.
